title: The Feedback Letter
brief: Meridian Care receives a letter from a patient's family: they were given 3 different discharge times on the same day, discharge information was missing pages, and their phone calls were not returned. This visit covers management system topics only. Clinical decisions, clinical standards, and law are outside its scope; the investigator does not judge clinical care. They ask for a written reply within 10 working days. You have 12 visit points.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

evidence.text: Feedback record FB-311 was logged the day the letter arrived with an owner.
5 similar letters this year about discharge times (FB-120 to FB-290) were answered individually; no corrective action was raised.
evidence.whyItMatters: Recurring feedback should lead to corrective action.

evidence.text: Discharge pack DP-2 for the ward is missing pages 3 and 4 in 6 of 10 packs in stock.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check the stock, not just one pack.

evidence.text: Discharge times were changed 3 times in the record on that day (entries 09:00, 13:00, 16:00) without a reason field.
evidence.whyItMatters: A reason would show where delays arise.

evidence.text: Call log shows 4 calls from the family; no return calls are recorded (log CL-17).
evidence.whyItMatters: Communication with customers must be handled as defined.

evidence.text: Nobody is named to return family calls on ward 4; staff "do it when they can".
evidence.whyItMatters: Assigning responsibility would make it reliable.

evidence.text: Print order PO-55 for discharge packs specified a 2-sided job; the printer delivered 1-sided, and no check on receipt.
evidence.whyItMatters: Externally provided products must be verified.

evidence.text: Feedback procedure requires a written reply within 10 working days.
Visiting hours sign is clear and current.
Feedback trends are an agenda item at management review.
evidence.whyItMatters: The organization has a forum for trends.

decisions.prompt: What should the reply to the family include?
options: An acknowledgment of each concern, what was found, what has been done (complete packs restocked, call responsibility assigned), what will change with dates, and a contact
An explanation that the ward was busy
A request to write to the ward directly
decisions.rationale: A reply that addresses each point and explains changes shows the feedback was used.

containment: Remove incomplete discharge packs from stock and check those given out recently
correction: Restock complete packs and reply to the family
cause: No receipt check of printed packs, no owner for family calls, and recurring feedback not escalated to corrective action
corrective: Add receipt checks for printed material, assign call responsibility, and escalate repeated feedback themes
effectiveness: Monitor discharge-related feedback for six months

debriefText.found: You linked the letter to supplies, communication, and trends.
debriefText.missed: Check stock, not just the pack the family received.
debriefText.falseFinding: A clear sign and flowers are not findings.
